SPARROW: region- and gene-based (co-)heritability analysis of rare variants

Source: R/sparrow.R
sparrow.Rd

Estimates the heritability explained by genes / regions (per variant category) and tests it using a saddlepoint approximation. Phenotypes are matched to the genotypes by IID, covariates are regressed out of the phenotypes here (and out of the genotypes inside the C++ code), and all bookkeeping that used to be manual (cov_df, binary_raw, the logistic null model, prs_mask) is done automatically.

Usage

sparrow(
  filename,
  pheno,
  out_file,
  covariates = NULL,
  annotation = NULL,
  annot_names = NULL,
  genes = NULL,
  alpha = c(-1, -0.5, 0),
  loco_prs = NULL,
  kvik_summaries = NULL,
  binary = FALSE,
  coher = FALSE,
  h2_without_prs = TRUE,
  prs_mask = NULL,
  do_windows = TRUE,
  chunk_size = 256,
  window_bp = 1e+06,
  max_window_chunks = 8,
  max_gene_snps = 512,
  min_gene_snps = 2,
  acatv_mac = 10,
  collapse_mac = 0,
  spa = TRUE,
  chr = NULL,
  n_threads = 0,
  batch_size = 16
)

Arguments

filename

PLINK prefix (.bed/.bim/.fam) holding rare variants and common SNPs.

pheno

Data frame or file: FID, IID, then one column per phenotype.

out_file

Output prefix. Writes <out_file> (regions), <out_file>.genes and <out_file>.windows.

covariates

Optional data frame or file: FID, IID, then numeric covariates (an intercept is added automatically; do not include one).

annotation

Optional 0/1 matrix or file (with header), one column per variant category (e.g. rare / common) and one row per .bim variant. A file may start with a column of variant IDs, which is matched to the .bim. NULL = one category with all variants.

annot_names

Category names (default: column names of annotation).

genes

Optional data frame or file: gene, chr, start, end (extra columns ignored). Must be on the same genome build as the .bim.

alpha

Heritability models tested; alpha[1] is used for the estimates.

loco_prs

Optional LDAK-KVIK Step 1 .loco.prs files: one per phenotype (character vector), or a matrix with one row per phenotype and one column per source.

kvik_summaries

Optional LDAK-KVIK Step 2 .summaries files, one per phenotype.

binary

TRUE if the phenotypes are 0/1 (1/2 coding is converted).

coher

TRUE to estimate co-heritability for all pairs of phenotypes.

h2_without_prs

With loco_prs: estimate h2 from y (TRUE) and use y - LOCO only for p-values. Recommended; see the supplement.

prs_mask

Advanced. Categories x PRS sources; which full PRS is subtracted in the window pass. Default: 0 if h2_without_prs, else 1.

do_windows

Estimate ~1 Mb windows and report window-calibrated h2 (h2_adj).

chunk_size, window_bp, max_window_chunks

Region and window sizes.

max_gene_snps, min_gene_snps

Genes are split into blocks of at most max_gene_snps variants; genes with fewer than min_gene_snps are skipped.

acatv_mac

Variants with MAC below this are collapsed into a burden in ACAT-V.

collapse_mac

Variance-component test: variants with MAC <= collapse_mac are summed into one pseudo-variant per category of each gene (as SAIGE-GENE+). 0 = off (default). ACAT-V still uses all variants individually.

spa

Compute saddlepoint p-values (FALSE = estimates only, much faster).

chr

Optional single chromosome to analyse.

n_threads

Number of threads (0 = RcppParallel default).

batch_size

Units per parallel batch (affects progress reporting only).

Value

Invisibly, a list with the output file names, the analysed traits and number of individuals, and the summary returned by the C++ code.

Examples

# \donttest{
# example data shipped with the package
dir <- system.file("extdata", package = "StratGWAS")

res <- sparrow(filename       = file.path(dir, "data"),
               pheno          = file.path(dir, "pheno_quant"),
               out_file       = file.path(tempdir(), "sparrow_example"),
               annotation     = file.path(dir, "annot"),
               genes          = file.path(dir, "genes"),
               loco_prs       = file.path(dir, "kvik.step1.loco.prs"),
               kvik_summaries = file.path(dir, "kvik.step2.summaries"),
               n_threads      = 2)
